content: 1. Tenofovir DF levels may increase when co-administered with sitagliptin due to reduced renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Sofosbuvir can elevate tenofovir DF levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for tenofovir-associated adverse reactions in patients receiving EPCLUSA with tenofovir DF-containing regimens. 4. Sotorasib decreases tenofovir DF levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 5. Stiripentol increases tenofovir DF levels or effects by inhibiting breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur. Monitor closely. 6. Streptomycin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Streptomycin reduces tenofovir DF elimination, increasing its levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Streptozocin and tenofovir DF co-administration is contraindicated due to increased nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid combining streptozocin with other nephrotoxic agents. 8. Sulindac and tenofovir DF co-administration increases each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 9. Tacrolimus and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Tafamidis increases tenofovir DF levels or effects by inhibiting BCRP in vitro. Dosage adjustments of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 11. Telavancin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Telavancin reduces renal clearance of tenofovir DF, increasing its levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tepotinib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its labeling. 13. Tipranavir and tenofovir DF co-administration increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tobramycin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Tobramycin reduces tenofovir DF elimination, increasing its levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tolmetin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Toxicity may result from co-administration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose NSAIDs. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 16. Tucatinib increases tenofovir DF levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. Monitor closely. 17. Ublituximab decreases tenofovir DF effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Vadadustat increases tenofovir DF levels or effects by increasing BCRP substrate exposure. Monitor for adverse effects of BCRP substrates and reduce their dose as per product labeling. 19. Valacyclovir increases tenofovir DF levels through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase tenofovir serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Valganciclovir increases tenofovir DF levels through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase tenofovir serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Vancomycin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Verapamil levels increase when co-administered with tenofovir DF due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely for potential toxicity. 23. Voclosporin and tenofovir DF co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Co-administration with nephrotoxic drugs may increase the risk of acute or chronic nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Zidovudine and tenofovir DF co-administration increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Perform pregnancy testing in individuals of childbearing potential before initiating therapy due to the potential risk of neural tube defects. Advise effective contraception during treatment and for 12 weeks after discontinuation due to the long half-life of efavirenz (EFV). Hormonal methods containing progesterone may have reduced effectiveness; always use barrier contraception in combination with other methods. 26. HIV-1-infected mothers should not breastfeed to avoid postnatal transmission of HIV-1. Limited data show that EFV, FTC, and tenofovir are present in human breast milk. The effects on milk production or the breastfed child are unknown. Mothers receiving the combination drug should not breastfeed due to the potential for HIV transmission, viral resistance, and adverse reactions in the infant. 27. Emtricitabine is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that, after phosphorylation, interferes with HIV viral DNA polymerase and inhibits viral replication. It is a cytosine analogue. 28. Tenofovir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that, after hydrolysis and phosphorylation, inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with AMP as a substrate. 29. Efavirenz is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) that binds to reverse transcriptase and blocks DNA polymerase activity without requiring phosphorylation for activity. 30. Administer the drug with water on an empty stomach, preferably at bedtime, to improve tolerability to nervous system symptoms. 31.
